newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SEES RECORD 1998 FLUE-CURED TOBACCO CROP.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SEES RECORD 1998 FLUE-CURED TOBACCO CROP.

text.p: Zimbabwe is set to increase its flue-cured tobacco crop by about 17 percent to a record 250 million kg in 1998, Zimbabwe Tobacco Association (ZTA) President Robert Webb said on Wednesday.

Webb said the industry was aiming for a record crop of 260 million kg this year but waterlogging had slashed output by almost 30 percent to 206 million kg, slightly more than the 201 kg produced in 1996.

"We hope to increase production to between 240 (million) and 250 million kg next year. We are hoping to increase production annually, that's the only way we can stay competitive in the world market," he said.
"This year we had the biggest crop ever produced but due to the heavy rains we are down about 30 percent," he told Reuters.
"We should be on target for a record crop next year," ZTA spokesman Lal Taylor added.
Zimbabwe is the world's fourth largest producer of tobacco after China, the U.S. and Brazil, and the second largest exporter of the yellow leaf after Brazil. China uses up all its crop.

Tobacco is one of Zimbabwe's biggest export earners, and Webb expected earnings from this year's annual tobacco auctions which started on Tuesday to be around Z$5.97 billion slightly over last year's Z$5.83 billion.
"We expect earnings this year to be up slightly on last year because the world tobacco price has come back a little," he said.
Opening prices at one of the main auction floors, the Tobacco Sales Floors owned mainly by white commercial farmers, averaged U.S.$2 a kilogram, 15 percent less than last year's prices.

They were slightly higher at U.S.$3.30 per kg at the country's new floors, the Boka Tobacco Auction Floors owned by black businessman Roger Boka who says they are the biggest tobacco sales floors in the world.

Webb said growers were concerned, however, at a 10 percent levy the government slapped last year on farmers and merchants which he said was squeezing producers' profits and a high duties levied on imported machinery.
